source.original_text: Let n>=3 and kappa>=4, let O have the existing normalized Borel Haar probability on full real O(n), and let A_O be the exact equation4 precision. Define the literal function p_O(v)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-v^T A_O v/2), with a real dimension-half exponent. For every x in Euclidean real n-space, put U=O_11 and r_O(x)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-(kappa+1-(kappa-1)U)||x||_2^2/4). Both O -> det(O)p_O(x) and O -> det(O)r_O(x) are absolutely integrable under that Haar probability, and their expectations are equal. All vectors, including zero and vectors already on the norm axis, are included. The claim is for these explicit functions; it does not identify p with a Gaussian probability density.

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with n ≥ 3 and every real κ with κ ≥ 4, let j₀ = 0 in Fin n, let O(n) be the full real orthogonal matrix group (including both determinant signs), and let μ be its normalized Haar probability measure, namely Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts O(n)). For O ∈ O(n), set
A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
Define the explicit real functions
p(O,v) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2π)^(n/2) · exp(−vᵀ A(O) v / 2), for real coordinate vectors v : Fin n → ℝ,
and
r(O,x) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2π)^(n/2) · exp(−(κ + 1 − (κ − 1)O₀₀) ‖x‖₂² / 4), for x ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
Here sqrt is the nonnegative real square root; (2π)^(n/2) uses the real exponent (n : ℝ)/2. The matrix products and quadratic form use the coordinates, and ‖x‖₂ is the actual Euclidean norm, not the coordinate supremum norm. Write vₓ = WithLp.ofLp x for the underlying coordinate vector of x.
Then for every x ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), both functions O ↦ det(O) p(O,vₓ) and O ↦ det(O) r(O,x) are absolutely Bochner L¹ integrable with respect to μ, and
∫_{O(n)} det(O) p(O,vₓ) dμ(O) = ∫_{O(n)} det(O) r(O,x) dμ(O).
The two L¹ assertions and the integral equality are simultaneous conclusions for each fixed x. The functions p and r are the literal displayed formulas; no probability-law construction or density characterization is assumed.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelRotation
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Reflection
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Norm-axis reduction of the literal signed Gaussian kernel average

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2.2 Ex58 and the following
O11 quadratic-form evaluation. Actual Gaussian-law/density identification,
spatial domination/Fubini and the original H(lambda) remain separate.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelRotation

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelAxis

private lemma exists_orthogonal_map {n : ℕ} (x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) :
    ∃ Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x = WithLp.ofLp y := by
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) :=
    (ℝ ∙ (x - y))ᗮ.reflection
  let b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ
  let Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ :=
    ⟨f.toMatrix b.toBasis b.toBasis, f.toMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup b b⟩
  have hm := LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr b.toBasis b.toBasis f.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap x
  have hfx : f x = y := Submodule.reflection_sub h
  refine ⟨Q, ?_⟩
  change (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x = WithLp.ofLp (f x) at hm
  exact hm.trans (congrArg WithLp.ofLp hfx)

private lemma axis_quadratic {n : ℕ} (κ t : ℝ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (j : Fin n) :
    (Pi.single j t) ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ Pi.single j t) =
      (κ + 1 - (κ - 1) * (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j j) * t ^ 2 / 2 := by
  rw [single_dotProduct]
  change t * ((singleBlockPrecision κ O) j ⬝ᵥ Pi.single j t) = _
  rw [dotProduct_single]
  simp only [singleBlockPrecision, Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.add_apply,
    Matrix.transpose_apply, Matrix.one_apply, ite_true, smul_eq_mul]
  ring

theorem signed_kernel_radial {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ :=
      fun O v => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-(v ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ v)) / 2)
    let r : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-(κ + 1 - (κ - 1) * (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0) *
            ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
      Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O (WithLp.ofLp x)) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
      Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O (WithLp.ofLp x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
  classical
  let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
  let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ :=
    fun O v => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-(v ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ v)) / 2)
  let r : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
    fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-(κ + 1 - (κ - 1) * (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0) *
          ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)
  change ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O (WithLp.ofLp x)) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧ _
  intro x
  let y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := PiLp.single 2 j0 ‖x‖
  have hnorm : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖ := by simp [y, PiLp.norm_single]
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ⟩ := exists_orthogonal_map x y hnorm
  have hy : WithLp.ofLp y = Pi.single j0 ‖x‖ := rfl
  have hr (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : p O (WithLp.ofLp y) = r O x := by
    dsimp only [p, r]
    rw [hy, axis_quadratic]
    congr 2
    ring
  have h := signed_kernel_rotation_invariant hn hκ
  change (∀ v : Fin n → ℝ, Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O v) (orthogonalHaar n)) ∧ _ at h
  have hrad : Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x) (orthogonalHaar n) :=
    (h.1 (WithLp.ofLp y)).congr (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O =>
      congrArg (fun z : ℝ => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * z) (hr O))
  refine ⟨h.1 (WithLp.ofLp x), hrad, ?_⟩
  have he := h.2 Q (WithLp.ofLp x)
  rw [hQ] at he
  calc
    _ = ∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O (WithLp.ofLp y) ∂orthogonalHaar n := he.symm
    _ = _ := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O =>
        congrArg (fun z : ℝ => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * z) (hr O)

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelAxis

steps.title: Choose the true Euclidean norm-axis point
steps.text: For any Euclidean x, take y=||x||_2 e1. Its Euclidean norm is ||x||_2 because that scalar is nonnegative. This holds also at zero and when x already equals y. Coordinates of y are exactly the single-coordinate vector with entry ||x||_2.
steps.lean: The public proof uses PiLp.single 2 j0 and PiLp.norm_single. hy identifies its WithLp.ofLp coordinates with Pi.single. No sup-norm substitution or division by ||x|| occurs.

steps.title: Produce the orthogonal map internally
steps.text: Equal-norm vectors are related by the reflection in the orthogonal complement of span(x-y). The existing canonical reflection theorem sends x to y uniformly, including x=y and x=y=0. The source uses transitivity implicitly; this is its explicit standard-background implementation.
steps.lean: Private exists_orthogonal_map calls the actual Submodule.reflection_sub. The reflection is a real linear isometry equivalence, with no new public witness or regularity assumption.

steps.title: Connect the isometry to the actual matrix action
steps.text: Use the canonical Euclidean orthonormal basis to represent that isometry as a matrix Q. The canonical isometry-to-matrix theorem proves Q belongs to full O(n), and the matrix-coordinate evaluation theorem gives Q times the coordinate vector of x equal to the coordinates of y. This is a proved adapter, not a changed action.
steps.lean: The same private provider calls LinearIsometryEquiv.toMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup and LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr in EuclideanSpace.basisFun. Its witness is an actual orthogonal matrix.

steps.title: Consume the identical fixed-Q Haar theorem
steps.text: Apply the previously compiled rotation/reflection-invariance theorem to this produced Q and the coordinates of x. Its actual matrix action is y, so the signed average at x equals the signed average at the norm-axis point. The same full Haar law and precision are used.
steps.lean: The public proof genuinely calls signed_kernel_rotation_invariant once, rewrites with the produced coordinate identity hQ, and reverses its equality. This is a real consumer of the unchanged canonical declaration.

steps.title: Evaluate the axis quadratic form exactly
steps.text: For a single-coordinate vector t e1, the quadratic form is t^2 times the first diagonal entry of the literal precision. That diagonal entry is (kappa+1-(kappa-1)U)/2. The extra factor1/2 in the Gaussian exponent produces exactly the denominator4. The square-root determinant and real normalization power are unchanged.
steps.lean: Private axis_quadratic uses single_dotProduct, dotProduct_single and the literal singleBlockPrecision entry. The public hr identity substitutes t=||x|| and proves the exact exponent arithmetic.

steps.title: Retain genuine finiteness on both sides
steps.text: The existing fixed-Q theorem already proves Haar L1 for every fixed coordinate vector. Apply it to x and to the produced y. Pointwise equality p_O(y)=r_O(x) transfers L1 to the displayed reduced formula, then integral equality follows. This concerns one fixed x at a time and exchanges no spatial integrals.
steps.lean: h.1 supplies both genuine L1 providers; Integrable.congr and integral_congr_ae use the actual hr identity. The two L1 conclusions accompany the final equality; original Gaussian-law/Fubini obligations are excluded.

lesson.lean_statement: Literal p and r local lets, actual Euclidean norm and coordinates; every vector and both Haar L1 conclusions are explicit.
lesson.lean_proof: Two reachable private providers produce the orthogonal coordinate witness and exact axis quadratic evaluation. The public proof consumes the existing fixed-Q invariant/L1 theorem and discharges the full literal norm-axis identity.
